title: No-flow days at 137 US drying stream gauges did not rise past their 1999-2017 level in 2018-2025, except in western deserts and mountains; P/PET did not explain the shifts
abstract: Zipper et al. (2021) found that annual no-flow days at US non-perennial stream gauges changed in 1980-2017: drying in the south and west and wetting in the north. We tested if these changes continued in eight new climate years, 2018-2025. We used USGS NWIS daily discharge for 9,067 GAGES-II gauges and the same no-flow rule. We reproduced the published Mann-Kendall trend class for 96.8% of 539 matched gauges. Of 541 gauges with test data, 137 had a drying trend. In 2018-2025, 74% of these stayed above their 1980-2017 mean, but only 52% rose past their 1999-2017 mean (p = 0.73; median +1.5 days per year). In a placebo split inside the published period, 68% of drying gauges continued past their recent level in 2010-2017 (p = 0.002), so the stall is new. Wetting gauges continued a little (67% lower than their 1999-2017 mean, p = 0.002). Drying continued in the Western Deserts (13 of 16 gauges) and less in the Western Mountains. The 1999-2017 mean gave the lowest mean absolute error (29.0 days per year). Sen-trend extension (32.5) and a per-gauge model with basin precipitation over Thornthwaite PET (33.1) were worse. The climate model explained a median 33% of yearly variance. After the climate adjustment, 46% of drying trends and 70% of wetting trends stayed significant, and in 2018-2025 the trend gauges kept their offsets from the climate forecast. Thus, the changes acted as persistent level shifts that current- and prior-year P/PET did not explain. Limitations: only eight test years, near-zero discharge measurement sensitivity, most gauges are not reference gauges, temperature-only PET, and spatial clustering (HUC-2 cluster intervals include zero for some forecast differences). Code, derived public-domain tables, figures and source hashes are included. The CC BY-NC-SA Zipper et al. release is not bundled.

display.caption: Mean annual no-flow-day anomaly (relative to each gauge's 1980-2017 mean) for gauges with a drying, wetting or no 1980-2017 Mann-Kendall trend (left), and residuals after a per-gauge P/PET model fitted on 1980-2017 (right). Shaded: test climate years 2018-2025 (541 gauges).

Change in mean no-flow days from 1999-2017 to 2018-2025 per gauge, by region and 1980-2017 trend class. Bars are medians. Drying gauges rose further only in the Western Deserts and Western Mountains (and slightly in the South Great Plains).

Mean absolute error of four forecasts of each gauge's 2018-2025 mean no-flow days, all gauges and by region. The 1999-2017 mean was best overall; trend extension was better only in the Eastern Forests and north Great Plains.
